I wanted to like Magic John. Clean install, slick marketing, big promises. What I got instead was two screen protectors that cracked on their own and a customer service policy that hides behind “industry standard” excuses.

The first protector chipped almost immediately—within a day or two of application—right near the top speaker. I hadn’t dropped my phone, slammed it down, or hit it against anything. It just… cracked. Worse, the chip was sharp enough that it nearly cut me. That’s not just disappointing; that’s unsafe.
When I contacted customer service, they were reasonably quick to respond, but immediately hit me with “we need a photo.” Fine, I get wanting proof—except my phone is my camera. Removing the already-fractured protector to document it caused it to break further, which they then used as justification to deny any help. They told me there was “nothing they could do” and that needing a photo was an “industry standard.” It isn’t. It’s just their policy, and a convenient one at that.
They eventually sent a second protector. Two months later, it cracked too—again without any drop or impact—this time at the bottom edge near the swipe area. I didn’t even notice it immediately, until it sliced my thumb. A screen protector that fails silently and cuts you is not protecting anything.
At this point, I’m done. Two spontaneous cracks, zero accountability, and a rigid support process that ignores obvious real-world use. If your product can’t survive normal handling and your solution is “sorry, no photo, no help,” that’s not quality—that’s a liability.

Save your money. There’s no magic here—just brittle glass and corporate shrugging.
